petty

/PET-ee/ — sounds like 'pet' + 'ee' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Petty is of very little importance; too small to deserve the fuss.

Their friendship nearly ended over a petty disagreement about a borrowed pencil.

Example

The two vice presidents were supposed to plan the company's future. Instead, they spent the entire meeting on petty disputes: whose name should appear first on the memo, and who got the slightly larger office.

Petty matters are of very little importance. A 'minor' issue is simply small; calling something petty adds a sting of criticism, suggesting the people involved should know better than to care.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

trivial: Trivial means something is of little real value or importance — a trivial detail is simply unimportant, and saying so passes no judgment on anyone. Petty adds a criticism of the people involved: a petty dispute is not just small; it makes those who fuss over it look small-minded.

minor: Minor means lesser in size or seriousness — a minor repair, a minor delay. It is a neutral measurement that passes no verdict. Petty goes further: calling a concern petty says it is too small to deserve the fuss and that caring about it makes a person look small.

trifling: Trifling describes something so small it hardly matters, often with a light, almost amused shrug. Petty is harsher: a petty complaint is not just tiny — the word scolds the complainer, hinting that a grown person should be above caring about it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

major: great in importance or scale

momentous: of enormous importance or consequence

Where it sits · how little it deserves attention — modest → petty → negligible

modest vs. petty: Modest is weaker than petty as a put-down — a modest concern is simply limited in size, without petty's sting of small-mindedness.

negligible vs. petty: Negligible is stronger than petty — a petty matter is unimportant but still gets attention, while a negligible one is so tiny it can be ignored entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — petit

root — petit: small (French)

Put it together

Put it together: French petit means 'small.' Petty took the idea of physical smallness and applied it to importance — matters too small to deserve the fuss they receive.

Use the root in a new word: petite

Use the root in a new word: petite: The petite dancer moved so lightly she seemed to float across the stage.
